stories.title: Sudan war: 318 RSF fighters defect to army in latest blow to paramilitary
stories.summary: Sudan’s army says 318 Rapid Support Forces fighters, including four commanders, have defected and joined its ranks in the latest apparent surrender by paramilitary personnel. The move comes as defections increase and fighting continues to devastate the country more than three years into the war.

stories.title: Trump says North Korea has '57 very powerful nuclear weapons'
stories.summary: Trump's comments come just days after he announced that he had ordered US forces to scale back joint military drills with South Korea, which he said sent an "inappropriate and hostile" signal to Pyongyang.
article_sentences: Trump's comments come just days after he announced that he had ordered US forces to scale back joint military drills with South Korea, which he said sent an "inappropriate and hostile" signal to Pyongyang.

US President Donald Trump on Wednesday suggested there was a rather menacing reason to be grateful for his good working relationship with Kim Jong Un - North Korea's "57 very powerful nuclear weapons."

Speaking to reporters from outside the White House, Trump confirmed he would be meeting with Kim later this year as he was asked about his recent hints regarding his communications with the North Korean leader.
While he refused to say whether the pair were exchanging letters, he said he gets "along with him very well."
"And you know what, the fact that I get along with him, that's a good thing not a bad thing.
Should have never allowed it to happen," he said, adding: "If I were president, I wouldn't have allowed it.
"I know Kim Jong Un very well, and he's going to be fine," he continued.
"As long as we have a smart president, he's going to be fine.
If we have a dumb president, then he's probably not going to be so fine."
Trump gave no further details on the planned meeting with Kim, which would be their first since Trump's first term in the White House.

The president's comments come just days after he announced that he had ordered US forces to scale back "costly" joint military drills with South Korea, which he said sent an "inappropriate and hostile" signal to Pyongyang.
